metadata.description: General-purpose AI tooling by Michael Pesin: skills and agents usable in any codebase, by anyone

plugins.name: repo-mapper
plugins.description: Replace /init with a token-lean, progressively-disclosed repo index (AGENTS.md + docs/agents/) usable by Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini

plugins.name: design-critic
plugins.description: Adversarial DESIGN reviewer agent (not a general critical-thinking aid): attacks the assumptions of plans, specs, and architectures, hunts failure modes, steelmans simpler alternatives, returns severity-ranked findings and a verdict

plugins.name: lean-talk
plugins.description: Lean responses and documents (/lean-talk:lean-talk), applied as the text is written, never as a rewrite pass, plus /lean-talk:lean-edit to rewrite an existing file or pasted text by the same rules: whole sentences with every fact kept, filler and hedging cut, the answer in the first line, lists for parallel items, tables for repeated fields, a budget per document section. Grammar and articles stay

plugins.name: dev-flow
plugins.description: Plan, implement, review and QA-impact flow run by subagents (/dev-flow:dev-plan, /dev-flow:dev-implement, /dev-flow:dev-qa-impact, /dev-flow:load-flow, /dev-flow:clear-flow; also implements dev-debug's fix plans), or the whole flow on autopilot with /dev-flow:orchestrate (a critical orchestrator subagent rules at every gate against the specs and acceptance criteria and escalates what they do not settle) and guarded by cross-platform hooks: commits per package and fix round, pushes and opens the PR on request from the main session, no subagent pushes/PRs/commits, no force push/discard/comments/merges/publishing, per-agent and per-package write limits, build/test evidence required before an implementer may finish, working-tree change detection, gate notifications; the guards follow the session that runs the flow, so other sessions on the same checkout are not blocked

plugins.name: dev-debug
plugins.description: Diagnose a bug before anyone changes code (/dev-debug:dev-debug): a clean-slate, read-only debugger subagent reproduces the failure, tests hypotheses against the code and git history, and writes diagnosis.md with evidence, blast radius and confidence; you confirm the cause (or ask for an independent second opinion) and the diagnosis becomes a regression-test-first fix plan for dev-flow; under /dev-flow:orchestrate the orchestrator agent takes the gate for you

plugins.name: dev-flow-panel
plugins.description: Companion band above the prompt for dev-flow and dev-debug: buttons that start each skill and a colour-coded view of the current stage (planning, approved, implementing, Claude review, your review, QA impact, done, blocked; a bug from dev-debug shows diagnosing and confirm cause instead of planning)
